title: Graphing a Reflected Cube Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = -cbrt(x) by starting with the standard cube root graph y = cbrt(x) and applying an appropriate reflection.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \sqrt[3]{x} \text{ reflected across x-axis};\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } (-\infty, \infty),\quad \text{Inflection point / intercept: } (0, 0)

steps.title: Identify the Reflection Transformation
steps.explanation: Multiplying the parent cube root function y = cbrt(x) by -1 reflects its graph across the x-axis (or equivalently across the y-axis, since cbrt(-x) = -cbrt(x)).
steps.why: For any odd function, reflection across the x-axis coincides with reflection across the y-axis.

steps.title: Determine the Domain, Range, and Symmetry
steps.explanation: The function is defined and strictly decreasing across all real numbers, with a vertical tangent at its origin inflection point (0, 0).
steps.why: Negating a strictly increasing bijection on R produces a strictly decreasing bijection on R.

steps.title: Plot Key Symmetric Points
steps.explanation: The curve descends from the second quadrant through (-8, 2) and (-1, 1), crosses the origin (0, 0) vertically, and continues into the fourth quadrant through (1, -1) and (8, -2).
steps.why: Evaluating at perfect cubes x = -8, -1, 0, 1, 8 gives exact integer coordinates.
